record.binding_note: a single /128 is the hard ceiling: there is no routed prefix, so anything needing more than one address needs another instance.

record.confidence_note: shape, the /128 statement, the fair-use bandwidth line, the two prices and the billing periods are quoted from the vendor's product page read. The cart is the product page itself: the 'Order Now' button is an anchor to the same product path and the add-to-cart is a Livewire action, so there is no GET cart URL to give a buyer.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'MCI-N-B (IPv6 Only) Starting at €1.25 per month ... 1 Shared vCPU ... 1024 MiB RAM ... 20 GB HDD ... 10000 Mbps (10Gbps) Fair Use bandwidth ... IPv6-only environment' and 'MCI-N-C (IPv6 Only) Starting at €1.25 per quarter ... 384 MiB RAM ... 5 GB HDD'

quoted: 'Only IPv6 is supported; you cannot access any IPv4 internet.' and 'Each instance is assigned one dedicated IPv6 address (/128).' and 'No data safety guarantee - Please ensure your own backups'
quoted BGP terms: 'Up to 20 BGP routes with downstream support' and 'A ticket must be submitted to enable the BGP session.'
the cart page renders 'Your cart is empty' at 200, so the store is live; the add-to-cart itself is a Livewire wire:click action on the product page, not a link with a product id

record.notes: The best RAM-per-euro among the rows whose cart can be found, and the only one that states the delivery form outright: a single /128. That is enough for a WireGuard endpoint or a monitor (one address, every port open) but it is not a routed prefix, so the 'every port on the guest's own address' advantage stops at one address. The caveats stack: no data-safety guarantee, no published traffic ceiling, no published payment rails, and an entity that the store does not name on any page reached. BGP up to 20 routes on a /128 is a routing-lab feature rather than a requirement. Not established: who operates Axivora, the registration and checkout fields, payment rails, card hold, and whether 'per quarter' on MCI-N-C is the minimum term for MCI-N-B too.

record.interface_detail: IPv6-only instance with one dedicated /128; up to 20 BGP routes available on a ticket
record.tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; a web store with an account area; BGP session on request by ticket
record.chaining: an IPv6-only box with a routed /128 and optional BGP at USD 0.47 a month, which is the cheapest genuinely IPv6-only machine among evaluated providers that is in stock and sold by a company that exists in a state register.

limits.value: no byte allowance; 10 Gbps port under a fair-use policy, so the throttle is discretionary and has no published ceiling
one dedicated IPv6 address as a /128, and no IPv4 at all: 'you cannot access any IPv4 internet'

record.binding_note: a single /128 with no IPv4 means anything that needs to reach an IPv4-only host, including most package mirrors and most APIs, is unreachable without a NAT64 or proxy in front.

identity_cost.detail: email, first name, last name and password only. The registration form source carries exactly these fields plus a terms tick: email, first_name, last_name, password, password_confirm, tos. No card field, no phone field, no address field and no national ID field at registration. Whether a card is required at the payment step was not established, because the store was not taken to checkout.

record.reliability_note: The vendor states on the product itself 'No data safety guarantee — Please ensure your own backups'; the company was incorporated on 13 October 2025, so it is under a year old at the time of reading; no uptime figure published.
record.confidence_note: shape, price, the /128, the no-IPv4 rule, the fair-use bandwidth, the stock state and the registration fields are quoted from the vendor's own pages read; the legal entity, its status and its incorporation date are quoted from the Companies House record read. The billing cycle is the one soft field: the group page says 'per quarter' for this plan and 'per month' for the larger MCI-N-B, while the product page prints EUR 1.25 with no cycle. Both readings are recorded in the arithmetic.

extras.price_arithmetic: Two readings, both recorded. As quarterly: EUR 1.25 / 3 = EUR 0.4167 a month, / 0.89342 EUR per USD = USD 0.4664 a month, and EUR 1.25 = USD 1.3991 out of pocket every quarter. As monthly: EUR 1.25 / 0.89342 = USD 1.3991 a month. The group page states 'per quarter' for MCI-N-C and 'per month' for MCI-N-B, which is the reading used for the headline figure. Rate from api.frankfurter.app read 2026-10-24, rate date 2026-10-23. VPS billing: the machine bills whether it runs or not.
